To prove the theorem `lg_target`, we need to show that the category of finite groups, `FintypeCat`, has colimits of shape `CategoryTheory.SingleObj G` for any finite group `G`. This is equivalent to showing that the category of finite types (or finite groups) admits colimits indexed by a single object — which is essentially saying that it has all coproducts and coequalizers (since colimits of shape `SingleObj G` are just coproducts and coequalizers).

The proof proceeds as follows:

1. **Understand the shape**: The shape `CategoryTheory.SingleObj G` refers to a category with a single object and no non-identity morphisms. Colimits of this shape in a category are simply coproducts (when there are no morphisms) or coequalizers (if we consider more general diagrams), but in this case, since there's only one object, the colimit reduces to an object itself.

2. **Use known results**: Since `FintypeCat` is a finitely complete and cocomplete category (as it is equivalent to the category of finite sets and functions), it has all colimits. In particular, it has coproducts (disjoint unions of finite sets) and coequalizers (which exist because the category is closed under quotients).

3. **Apply the appropriate lemma**: The theorem can be proven using the fact that if a category has all finite colimits, then it has colimits of shape `SingleObj G` for any finite group `G`. This is a special case of the general result that if a category has finite colimits, then it has colimits of shape any finite category.

Thus, the proof relies on the fact that `FintypeCat` is cocomplete and uses properties of finite colimits to conclude the existence of colimits of shape `CategoryTheory.SingleObj G`.
